thread:
olivia: Quick live thread from today's all-hands runtime segment. Capturing the key clarifications we promised: batching behavior, KV cache policy, and kernel-v4 canary plan.
raj: two clarifications: 1) does "adaptive batching" mean per-worker only or cross-worker pooling? 2) what escapes do SLA customers have to avoid batching?
tereza: proposal: start per-worker adaptive microbatching. Allow SLA bypass via X-Request-Priority header. Cross-worker pooling later.
carl: ops note: we need concrete p95 bounds if we enable adaptive batching. Recommend target p95 <= 120ms for hosted during normal load; SLA routes bypass batching.
olivia: agreed. Add a console toggle for max_batch_size and a priority bypass flag. Small config stub:
```
batching:
  mode: adaptive
  max_batch_size: 48
  priority_header: X-Request-Priority
```
raj: KV cache question 1: default TTL is 5m today. Ops asked about hot-prefix retention. Suggest LRU with per-tenant memory caps and a hot-score extension to TTL.
tereza: action: ops will run a 10-day experiment increasing hot-prefix TTL to 20m on a few clusters and report cost + p95 impact. If cost delta < 7% and p95 improves, we enable.
olivia: kernel-v4 timeline?
carl: kernel-v4 microbench suite finishes Monday. If green, stage-1 canary (10% non-SLA) in 10 days, stage-2 (50%) two weeks later, and full roll by end of quarter if no regressions. Telemetry gating includes model-determinism samples and quality evals.
ops-bot: Notes uploaded: https://redwood.internal/notes/allhands-2690011111. :white_check_mark:
olivia: thanks 1 please file the small RFCs: batching config + kernel thresholds. I'll consolidate. Ping me for blockers.
